title: Facepalm Emoji 🤦 Meaning: SMH, Disbelief and Cringe
description: 🤦 is a hand over the face: “I can’t believe this,” whether aimed at someone else’s blunder or your own. Learn how the facepalm emoji is used and misused.
summary: 🤦 shows a person pressing a hand to their face. It expresses exasperation, disbelief or embarrassment at something foolish, the emoji form of “SMH” or “seriously?” People use it about their own mistakes as often as other people’s, so it can be self-deprecating or critical depending on the target.
meaning: A facepalm is what happens when words fail in the face of stupidity. The emoji captures that moment: a head dropped into a hand because something is too dumb, too obvious or too awkward to address directly. It reacts to bad jokes, avoidable errors, tone-deaf comments and news headlines that make you despair a little. Sometimes the only honest response is to cover your eyes.

The gesture was internet shorthand long before it was an emoji. People typed *facepalm* in forums and chats, and reaction images of the pose, including a famous still of a starship captain from television, circulated for years. Unicode added 🤦 in 2016, in the same release as the shrug, and it quickly replaced the typed-out word. The emoji made a well-worn joke available in a single tap.

Direction matters. Aimed at yourself, it is endearing: “sent the email without the attachment again 🤦.” It admits a mistake with humor and invites sympathy. Aimed at another person, it is a judgment, and its harshness depends on the relationship. Friends can facepalm at each other all day. From a parent, boss or stranger, it can feel condescending. The same symbol can comfort or sting depending on who is on the receiving end.

It differs from anger. 🤦 is weary rather than furious, more “why am I like this” or “why are they like this” than “how dare you.” That makes it a common reaction to secondhand embarrassment, when you cringe on someone else’s behalf, and to puns so bad they deserve a groan. In each case the feeling is closer to a sigh than to a shout.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: The self-directed facepalm is the everyday one: forgetting a birthday, walking into a glass door, texting the wrong person. Replying to a friend’s story with 🤦 means “oh no, you didn’t,” usually with affection. It also answers dad jokes and puns, where the groan is the intended reward. Sending it about your own blunder invites the other person to laugh with you.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Commenters use 🤦 under fail videos, misinformed opinions and public figures’ gaffes. Often it appears with 😂 to show the mistake is funny, or alone to signal real dismay. On posts where someone shares an embarrassing story, it expresses shared cringe rather than criticism. The more of them in a row, the deeper the collective despair.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is common and accepted for owning up to small slips, such as “wrong link, sorry 🤦.” That use can actually build goodwill because it shows humility. Reacting with 🤦 to a colleague’s question or mistake in a public channel is another matter; it broadcasts that you think they were foolish.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: A facepalm from someone you like usually means you made them groan, which in flirting is often a good thing. If they send it after your cheesy joke with a laughing emoji, they are enjoying the banter. If it follows something you were serious about, they may be gently telling you it missed the mark.

examples.text: Showed up to the meeting a day early 🤦
examples.meaning: Embarrassed about their own silly mistake.
Disbelief at someone else’s obviously bad decision.

examples.text: Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field 🤦
examples.meaning: Groaning at a deliberately terrible pun.
Cringing at an awkward slip of the tongue.

examples.text: They cancelled the flight, rebooked it, and cancelled again 🤦

examples.meaning: Teasing a friend who messed up something simple.

combos.meaning: Something is so dumb it is funny.

confusedWith.difference: 🤷 means “I don’t know” or “whatever.” 🤦 means “I can’t believe this happened.” One lacks an answer; the other has seen the answer and is dismayed.
🙄 shows annoyance and contempt, often toward a person’s attitude. 🤦 is more about disbelief or embarrassment at a mistake and is easier to turn on yourself.
🫣 covers the face but peeks through fingers, mixing embarrassment with curiosity. 🤦 hides the face completely in defeat, with no desire to keep watching.

avoid: Do not react with it to someone’s sincere question, which makes them feel stupid for asking.
Avoid directing it at a colleague’s error in a group channel.
Leave it out of responses to serious bad news, where exasperation can look like blame.
design: A person is drawn from the chest up with eyes closed or downcast and one hand flat against the forehead or covering part of the face. Platforms vary in which hand is used and how much of the face it hides. A gender-neutral base exists alongside woman 🤦‍♀️ and man 🤦‍♂️ versions, each available in five skin tones.

faqs.q: What does 🤦‍♀️ mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She is exasperated or embarrassed, either with herself or with something you said. After a joke it is a playful groan. After you admit a mistake it means “oh no.” Check whether a laughing emoji comes with it; that tells you she is amused rather than annoyed.

faqs.q: What does 🤦‍♂️ mean from a guy?
faqs.a: The same thing: disbelief, cringe or “I messed up.” Guys often use it to laugh at their own blunders. If he sends it about something you did, he is teasing unless the conversation is tense, in which case he may be frustrated.

Yes, they overlap closely. SMH stands for “shaking my head,” and both it and the facepalm express disappointment or disbelief at something foolish. The emoji adds a note of embarrassment and is used about oneself more readily than SMH.

When aimed at another person, it can be. It implies they did something dumb. Between friends that is ordinary teasing, but toward strangers, colleagues or someone already upset, it reads as condescending. Using it about your own mistakes is never rude.
